name: Cyion Smith
strengths: Smith plays with real length at 6-2 — covers ground in a few strides when the ball leaves the hash.
Smith stays stacked on the perimeter as a deep-third / alley safety and does not panic when receivers stem at him.
Smith finishes pursuit angles downhill and is willing to stick his face in the run after the catch.
weaknesses: Smith still needs to fill out the 6-2 / 175 frame before he can win with mass against SEC tight ends in the box.
comparison: Smith comps to Justin Simmons — 6-2 rangy free-safety mold; length, center-field range, and eyes over the top before the frame fills.
projection: Smith projects as develop in the Florida safety room under Collins, earn special-teams / package snaps early, then compete for FS/nickel work — starter upside in the back end as he adds 15–20 pounds.
schemeFit: Smith fits a length-first safety room that asks the deep defender to range over the top and fill the alley without guessing.
insiderNotes: Vault film desk on Cyion Smith soph-season Hudl (2:33): Blountstown S tagged on the perimeter with an orange spotlight — long strider at 6-2 / 175, range to the football, calm feet when receivers stem.
